# Annual Leave Policy (Republic of Ireland)

Jurisdiction: Ireland | Effective date: 1 January 2026 | Version 2.0 | Owner: HR Advisory Team


## 1. Statutory Entitlement

Under the Organisation of Working Time Act 1997, employees are entitled to 4 working weeks of
paid annual leave per leave year. Entitlement is calculated by whichever of the following gives the
greater result: (a) 4 working weeks where the employee works at least 1,365 hours in the leave
year; (b) one third of a working week per calendar month of at least 117 hours worked; or (c) 8% of
hours worked, subject to a maximum of 4 working weeks.


## 2. Public Holidays

Ireland has 10 public holidays. Public holidays are separate from, and additional to, the annual
leave entitlement. An employee required to work on a public holiday is entitled to an additional day's
pay, a paid day off within a month, or an additional day of annual leave.


## 3. Carry-Over and Payment in Lieu

Annual leave should normally be taken within the leave year. With the employee's consent, leave
may be taken within 6 months of the following year. Payment in lieu of untaken statutory leave is
only permitted on termination of employment.


## 4. Notice Requirements for Booking Leave

Employees in Ireland must submit leave requests at least 4 weeks in advance for requests longer
than 3 days, and at least 1 week in advance for shorter requests. The employer must take family
responsibilities and available rest into account when approving leave.

# Ireland Remote Working Policy - Contrast Document

Document ID: DOC-004

Jurisdiction: IE

Effective date: 2026-07-01

Document type: HR Policy

Source URL: https://example.com/hr/ie-remote-working-policy


## 1. Scope

This policy applies to employees whose contractual work location is in Ireland. Requests are handled under the
employer's Ireland-specific process.


## 2. Requests

Employees submit remote-working requests through the HR portal. Managers consider business requirements,
team collaboration, data security and the employee's circumstances.


## 3. Review

The policy may be reviewed when Irish employment requirements or company arrangements change.

# Remote and Hybrid Working Policy

Document ID: DOC-002

Jurisdiction: UK

Effective date: 2026-06-15

Document type: HR Policy

Source URL: https://example.com/hr/remote-hybrid-working-policy


## 1. Purpose

This policy defines principles for remote and hybrid working for UK employees and should be read with the
employment contract and applicable security and data-protection policies.


## 2. Eligibility and Approval

Hybrid working is available where a role can be performed effectively away from the office. Approval considers
role requirements, team collaboration, customer needs, security and individual circumstances.

Managers may require office attendance for meetings, training, customer activities or other legitimate business
reasons.


## 3. Home Working

Employees working from home are responsible for maintaining a safe and suitable workspace and reporting
material health and safety concerns.

Company equipment must be protected from loss, unauthorised access and damage. Confidential information
must not be accessible to unauthorised people.


## 4. Expenses

Reasonable approved business expenses incurred while working remotely may be reimbursed under the
company's expenses rules. Ordinary household costs are not automatically reimbursable.


## 5. Review

The policy is reviewed at least annually and may be updated sooner if legislation, business requirements or
security standards change.

# Annual Leave Policy (United Kingdom) Jurisdiction: United Kingdom | Effective date: 1 April 2026 | Version 3.2 | Owner: HR Advisory Team ## 1. Statutory Entitlement All full-time employees are entitled to a minimum of 5.6 weeks (28 days) of paid annual leave per leave year, which may include the 8 English bank holidays. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement calculated as 5.6 times their normal working week, capped at 28 days. ## 2. Leave Year and Carry-Over The company leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March. Employees may carry over a maximum of 5 unused days into the next leave year with line manager approval. Carried-over days must be used before 30 June or they are forfeited. Statutory leave that could not be taken due to maternity leave or long-term sickness may be carried over for up to 18 months. ## 3. Sickness During Annual Leave If an employee falls sick during booked annual leave and provides a fit note covering the period, the affected days are reclassified as sick leave and the annual leave days are returned to the employee's balance. ## 4. Notice Requirements for Booking Leave Employees must give notice of at least twice the length of the leave requested. For example, a request for 5 days of leave requires at least 10 working days' notice. The company may refuse a request by giving counter-notice equal to the length of the leave requested. ## 5. # Disciplinary Procedure (United Kingdom)

Jurisdiction: United Kingdom | Effective date: 1 June 2026 | Version 4.1 | Owner: Employment Law
Team


## 1. Purpose and Scope

This procedure follows the Acas Code of Practice on disciplinary and grievance procedures. It
applies to all employees who have completed their probationary period.


## 2. Stages of the Procedure


### 2.1 Stage One - Verbal Warning

Issued for minor misconduct. Remains active on file for 6 months.


### 2.2 Stage Two - First Written Warning

Issued for repeated minor misconduct or a more serious first offence. Remains active for 12
months.


### 2.3 Stage Three - Final Written Warning

Issued where a written warning is already active, or for serious misconduct. Remains active for 12
months.


### 2.4 Stage Four - Dismissal

Dismissal with notice, or without notice in cases of gross misconduct. Only a director or head of
department may authorise dismissal.


## 3. Gross Misconduct

Examples include theft, fraud, physical violence, serious breach of health and safety rules, serious
insubordination, and unauthorised disclosure of confidential client data. Gross misconduct may
result in summary dismissal without notice or payment in lieu of notice, following a fair investigation
and hearing.


## 4. Right to be Accompanied

Employees have the statutory right to be accompanied at any disciplinary hearing by a colleague or
a trade union representative. The request must be reasonable.


## 5. Appeals

An employee may appeal any disciplinary decision in writing within 5 working days of receiving the
outcome. Appeals are heard by a manager not previously involved, and the appeal decision is final.

# Sample UK Employment Contract

Document ID: DOC-001

Jurisdiction: UK

Effective date: 2026-04-01

Document type: Employment Contract

Source URL: https://example.com/hr/uk-employment-contract


## 1. Employment

The employee is employed as a Senior Software Engineer. The normal place of work is the employer's
Manchester office, with hybrid working permitted under the Remote and Hybrid Working Policy.

Employment is subject to UK law and the terms of this contract.


## 2. Working Hours

Normal working hours are 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday. Additional reasonable hours may occasionally
be required, subject to applicable UK working-time requirements.


## 3. Annual Leave

The holiday year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Employees receive 25 days of annual leave per holiday
year plus UK bank holidays.

Leave should normally be requested through the HR system at least 10 working days before the first day of
leave.


## 4. Notice

After probation, the employee must provide one month of written notice to resign. The employer will normally
provide one month of notice, subject to applicable statutory requirements.


## 5. Data and Confidentiality

The employee must protect confidential business information and personal data and follow information-security
and data-protection policies.

# UK Government Working Time Guidance - Practice Copy

Document ID: DOC-003

Jurisdiction: UK

Effective date: 2026-05-20

Document type: Government Guidance

Source URL: https://www.gov.uk/maximum-weekly-working-hours


## 1. Weekly Working Time

For most workers, average weekly working time should not normally exceed 48 hours. Workers can sometimes
agree to opt out of the 48-hour average limit, subject to applicable rules.


## 2. Rest

Workers generally have rights to rest breaks during the working day and daily and weekly rest periods. Exact
entitlement can depend on age, sector and working pattern.


## 3. Record Keeping

Employers should keep adequate records to demonstrate compliance with working-time requirements and apply
time-recording processes consistently.


## 4. Important Caveat

This practice document is synthetic material for RAG development and interview practice. It is not legal advice or
a substitute for checking current GOV.UK guidance or legislation.
